claim: GPUs, unlike CPUs, remain at high power draw even when visible compute/memory/communication activity is near zero -- a state the authors term 'execution-idle', directly measured via controlled benchmark on an Intel Xeon 6226R (CPU) vs NVIDIA L40S (GPU).
stance_target: idle GPU-hosted agent processes carry a disproportionate, non-intuitive energy/cost burden that justifies aggressive idle-detection policy
scope_conditions: GPU vs CPU power measurement, controlled matrix-multiplication benchmark
quoted_support: GPUs are becoming a major contributor to data center power, yet unlike CPUs, they can remain at high power even when visible activity is near zero. We call this state execution-idle.

claim: Among academic AI cluster jobs, online serving (handling live latency-sensitive requests -- the workload type closest to a running agent) is the most exposed regime: GPUs spend 61% of in-execution time in execution-idle, consuming 48% of energy during those idle intervals.
stance_target: idle time dominates GPU-hosted agent/serving workloads and is a primary cost/energy driver that auto-killing idle agents directly addresses
scope_conditions: large academic AI cluster, online serving workload category specifically
quoted_support: Among academic jobs, online serving (i.e., handling live latency-sensitive requests) is by far the most exposed regime: GPUs spend 61% of in-execution time in execution-idle, and 48% of energy is consumed during those intervals.

claim: Industry-derived serving trace replays show execution-idle ranging from 14% to 76% of time and 7% to 65% of energy depending on specific workload (Azure Chat, Azure Code, BurstGPT Chat, Qwen Reason, Qwen Chat), with Azure Code the worst offender and Qwen Chat the best.
stance_target: execution-idle exposure varies widely by workload type, meaning idle-kill thresholds should not be one-size-fits-all
scope_conditions: industry-derived serving trace replays (Azure Chat, Azure Code, BurstGPT Chat, Qwen Reason, Qwen Chat)
quoted_support: Low-activity periods account for 29%/17% of time/energy for Azure Chat, 76%/65% for Azure Code, 72%/52% for BurstGPT Chat, 18%/8% for Qwen Reason, and 14%/7% for Qwen Chat.

claim: Execution-idle onsets are most commonly preceded by PCIe transfers (48% of cases) and network-backed I/O / NIC-heavy activity (17%), suggesting the idle state is caused by software bottlenecks waiting on I/O rather than genuine computational completion.
stance_target: root cause of GPU idle time is I/O-bound waiting, a mechanism relevant to designing health-check / idle-detection signals for agent infrastructure
scope_conditions: academic AI cluster telemetry, root-cause attribution of execution-idle onset
quoted_support: By examining the activity immediately preceding execution-idle intervals, we find that they often follow PCIe transfers (48% of cases), network-backed I/O (17%), NVLink communication (2%), and other events, suggesting that execution-idle likely arises from software bottlenecks waiting on I/O.
